our_title: PT-Scotch tools return without MPI_Finalize on help/version; errorPrint never aborts the job
ran: Kit via $WORK/repro/run_all.sh <tree> <src tree> <out> (logs $WORK/repro/{pristine32,pristine64,patched32,patched64}.txt). Pristine 7.0.18 32/64: `mpirun --oversubscribe -np 2 <tool> -h|-V` for dgmap dgord dgscat dggath dgtst -> rc=1 and `... exited without calling "finalize"` for all 10; truncated part-1.grf: `timeout 30 mpirun -np 3 dgtst 'part-%r.grf'` -> `dgtst(1): ERROR: dgraphLoadDist: bad input (1)`, job killed by mpirun, rc=1. Patched (0003+0004) 32/64: all 10 rc=0; dgtst -> `MPI_ABORT was invoked on rank 1 in communicator MPI_COMM_WORLD`, rc=1.
read_only: the hang itself: Open MPI 5 kills the job on a non-zero exit, so the surviving ranks never hang here (needs a launcher that keeps the job alive, e.g. srun without KillOnBadExit)
severity_note: help/version exits only produce a spurious launcher error (rc 1); the error path hangs only with launchers that do not kill the job, hence low as in the review
review_accuracy: first half accurate and reproduced; the 'others can hang' claim is launcher dependent (not reproducible with Open MPI/PRRTE, which kills the job); its Fix line is what the series does
first_pass_critique: Right on both halves and honest about not reproducing the hang. It left MPI_Abort as a non-preferred sketch: the PT variant of the error-exit library already calls MPI_Initialized to print the rank, so it is MPI-aware by design and the abort belongs there (the sketch also lacked the MPI_Finalized guard, needed because MPI_Initialized stays true after MPI_Finalize). It did not note that usage is printed once per rank.

ran: mutate.sh (kit BLD-16) on data/m16x16.grf, anchor = the checkMap() call of the main loop. Pristine 7.0.18: (a) all vertices unmapped rc=0, (b) fixed vertex moved rc=0, (c) terminal 0 of the variable hypercube rc=0, (d) `parttab[5] = 5` on cmplt 5 -> `invalid mapping (2)` rc=1 (the 7.0.17 kit's (d) used 1000000 on archnum 3). Patched (0008) 32/64: (a) `invalid mapping (1)`, (b) `(3)`, (c) `(2)`, (d) `(2)`, all rc=1; unmutated check_scotch_graph_map rc=0.
severity_note: same as the review: the main sequential mapping test could not detect an unmapped or moved vertex
evidence: test_scotch_graph_map.c:95-96 'if (partval == -1)                            /* Unmapped vertex */\n      continue;' ; :102-103 'if ((flagval == 0) &&\n        (partval >= partnbr)) {' ; :254 'checkMap (vertnbr, parttab, archsiz, (archnum == (ARCHNBR - 1)) ? 1 : 0);' (no record of the preset fixed parts anywhere)
review_accuracy: accurate on the three gaps; its 'bound partval by the architecture size' is wrong for variable-sized architectures (SCOTCH_archSize (vhcub) = 1 while terminal numbers are binary-tree numbers, arch_vhcub.c:243-244): the right bound is 'is a terminal domain of the architecture', which SCOTCH_archDomTerm answers for every architecture (0 is rejected for vhcub, arch_vhcub.c:102-103; >= termnbr for cmplt, arch_cmplt.c:271)
first_pass_critique: Found the three gaps and tested mutations, but its preferred bound '2 * (vertnbr + 2)' for variable-sized architectures is an empirical constant with no meaning (labels are tree numbers whose depth depends on the strategy); SCOTCH_archDomTerm is the library's own definition of a valid terminal. It did not update G12's zero-load fixed-vertex case (which it could not know of) and did not notice that the old 'partnbr/flagval' parameters become dead once the architecture is passed.

our_title: gscat usage lists bare -i while the parser rejects -i without a number
ran: Kit via $WORK/repro/run_all.sh <tree> <src tree> <out> (logs $WORK/repro/{pristine32,pristine64,patched32,patched64}.txt). 7.0.18 pristine 32/64: `gscat -h` -> `-i<nbr> : Create a potentially imbalanced distribution with <nbr> vertices per process, remainder assigned to the last`; `gscat 3 m4x4.grf out-%r.grf -i` -> `invalid number of vertices in graph parts ''` rc=1; `-i2` rc=0.
severity_note: help text; same as the review
evidence: gscat.c:73 `"  -i<nbr> : Create a potentially imbalanced distribution with <nbr> vertices per process, remainder assigned to the last",`; :123 `if ((vertlocmin = (SCOTCH_Num) atoll (argv[i] + 2)) < 1)`; :218 `vertlocnbr = (procnum != (procnbr - 1)) ? vertlocmin : (vertglbnbr - (vertlocmin * (procnbr - 1)));`
upstream_change: cf82942a Fix gscat usage message [report R. Perry]: '-i<nbr>' with its argument, columns realigned

upstream_fix_review.details: gscat.c:72-74: '-i<nbr>' now shows its mandatory argument and the text matches the code (gscat.c:218 gives vertlocmin vertices to every part but the last, which takes the remainder; gscat.c:186-190 rejects too large values). The three lines are re-aligned. Header date bumped (14 oct 2026). Complete for BLD-23: the man page twin dgscat.1.txt:96-100 and p_p.tex already documented '-inbr' before. Not touched (outside BLD-23): dgscat.1.txt:98 still prints a literal LaTeX '\\textit{nbr}' (fixed by our 0007), and the gscat synopsis in dgscat.1.txt:9 and p_p.tex:479 omits the mandatory <nparts> parameter (new: PS3-G28-1). No behaviour change, no new defect.
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Same fix. Ours read '-i<nbr>  : Create an imbalanced distribution of <nbr> vertices per part (save for the last one)'; his says 'per process, remainder assigned to the last' and 'potentially imbalanced' (more exact: an exact value balances), at the cost of a 117-character usage line. Ours also lived in one commit with the gmap usage fix (CLI-20). His is as good; ours is dropped for gscat.

review_accuracy: accurate; the dgscat(1) man page and p_p.tex already document '-inbr ... For gscat only' (afe4479), so only the usage string drifted
first_pass_critique: Correct; its preferred wording ('each part having at least <num> vertices') is wrong: every part but the last gets exactly <nbr> vertices (C_graphScat's vertlocmin is 'Number of vertices for all processes but the last').
